---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m3p1t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxEpoch, MaxVer

VARIABLES leader, epoch, version, base, staged

vars == <<leader, epoch, version, base, staged>>

\* leader : current leader node, or "none"
\* epoch  : leadership epoch, strictly increases per election
\* version: live version stamp of the shared schedule record
\* base   : base version the most recent accepted commit built upon
\* staged : [Nodes -> Nat] version each node last read into staging

NoLeader == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ base \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ staged \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ base = 0
    /\ staged = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

Elect(n) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, base, staged>>

Read(n) ==
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![n] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, version, base>>

Commit(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ staged[n] = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ base' = staged[n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, staged>>

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, version, base, staged>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Read(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Commit(n)
    \/ StepDown

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    (version = 0) \/ (base = version - 1)

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxVer = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
Scenario: a hospital operating-room scheduler

Three scheduling nodes coordinate edits to a single shared master schedule
record for the operating rooms. Coordination uses leader election with
failover: at most one node holds leadership at a time, and each new leader
takes a strictly higher epoch number than any previous leader, so a stale
former leader is superseded the moment a successor is elected.

The shared record carries a version stamp. Before a node may commit an edit
it must first read the current version into its own staging slot. A commit
is accepted only from the current leader and only when the version it staged
still matches the record's live version -- that is, nobody else advanced the
record since it read. An accepted commit advances the version by one and
records the base version the edit was built upon.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a node may read the version and
then delay arbitrarily before attempting its commit. Meanwhile other commits
may advance the live version, leaving the slow node's staged version stale;
its commit is then refused until it reads again. A leader may also step down,
clearing leadership until the next election.

Actions: Elect (a node becomes leader at a strictly higher epoch), Read (a
node copies the live version into its staging slot), Commit (the current
leader whose staged version is still live advances the version by one and
stamps the base it built on), and StepDown (the current leader relinquishes
leadership).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the record has been edited at least once, the base
version stamped on the most recent accepted commit is exactly one less than
the live version, so no accepted edit was ever built on a stale read that
would silently discard an intervening update.

CONSTANTS Robots, Slots, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES leader, epoch, owner, claim, crashed

vars == <<leader, epoch, owner, claim, crashed>>

NoLeader == "none"
Free == "free"
NoClaim == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Robots \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Robots \cup {Free}]
    /\ claim \in [Robots -> Slots \cup {NoClaim}]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Robots

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ claim = [r \in Robots |-> NoClaim]
    /\ crashed = {}

Elect(n) ==
    /\ (n # leader \/ epoch < MaxEpoch)
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, claim, crashed>>

Grant(r, s) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ owner[s] = Free
    /\ claim[r] = NoClaim
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, crashed>>

Release(r) ==
    /\ claim[r] # NoClaim
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![claim[r]] = Free]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, crashed>>

Crash(r) ==
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, owner, claim>>

Reclaim(r) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ r \in crashed
    /\ claim[r] # NoClaim
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![claim[r]] = Free]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Robots : Elect(n)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : Grant(r, s)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Release(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Crash(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Reclaim(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OwnershipCoherent ==
    \A r \in Robots : claim[r] # NoClaim => owner[claim[r]] = r

=============================================================================
nl:
Scenario: a warehouse robot fleet

A fleet of three warehouse robots shares a small set of charging slots. A
leader node, chosen by leader election with failover, is the sole authority
that grants a slot to a robot; each new leader takes a strictly higher epoch
than the last so a superseded leader cannot keep granting.

The leader maintains an authoritative ownership table mapping each slot to
the robot that currently owns it (or "free"). Each robot also keeps a local
claim recording which slot, if any, it believes it holds. A grant sets both
sides at once: it marks a free slot as owned by a robot that holds no claim,
and records that robot's claim. A release clears both the ownership entry and
the robot's claim.

One participant can crash silently: a robot may crash without warning,
leaving its claim and its owned slot untouched. Because a crashed robot can
never release on its own, the leader may reclaim a slot -- but a correct
reclaim clears the authoritative ownership entry and the crashed robot's
stale claim together, so the slot can be safely granted to someone else
without two robots believing they hold it.

Actions: Elect (a node becomes leader at a strictly higher epoch), Grant (the
leader assigns a free slot to a claimless robot, setting ownership and the
robot's claim), Release (a robot clears its claim and frees its slot), Crash
(a robot crashes silently, retaining its claim and slot), and Reclaim (the
leader frees a crashed robot's slot and clears that robot's stale claim
together).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every robot that believes it holds a slot is in fact the
authoritative owner of that slot recorded by the leader, so no slot is ever
double-allocated to two robots at once.

    /\ slotVer \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ reqSlot \in [Players -> Slots \cup {NoReq}]
    /\ reqVer \in [Players -> 0..MaxVer]

    /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ slotVer = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ reqSlot = [p \in Players |-> NoReq]
    /\ reqVer = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ attempts = [p \in Players |-> 0]

    /\ reqSlot' = [reqSlot EXCEPT ![p] = s]
    /\ reqVer' = [reqVer EXCEPT ![p] = slotVer[s]]

    /\ slotVer[reqSlot[p]] = reqVer[p]
    /\ slotVer[reqSlot[p]] < MaxVer

    /\ slotVer' = [slotVer EXCEPT ![reqSlot[p]] = @ + 1]
    /\ reqSlot' = [reqSlot EXCEPT ![p] = NoReq]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqVer, attempts>>

    /\ slotOwner[reqSlot[p]] = Free
    /\ slotVer[reqSlot[p]] = reqVer[p]
    /\ slotVer[reqSlot[p]] < MaxVer

    /\ ~Committable(p)

    /\ slotVer[s] < MaxVer
    /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ slotVer' = [slotVer EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqSlot, reqVer, attempts>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Prepare(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Retry(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : Release(p, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A s \in Slots : (slotOwner[s] # Free) <=> (slotVer[s] % 2 = 1)

CONSTANTS
    Players = {p1, p2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxTry = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OwnedIffOdd
nl:
Scenario: a multiplayer game lobby matchmaker

A matchmaker hands out a small pool of match slots to players using optimistic
locking with retry. Each slot carries a monotonically advancing version
counter and an owner (a player, or "free"). A slot's version is even exactly
when the slot is free and odd exactly when it is owned; every successful claim
or release bumps the version by one.

To claim a slot a player first prepares: it reads the slot's current version
into a private request. Because messages can be reordered, an arbitrary amount
of activity may occur between preparing and committing, so the version the
player read may no longer be live. A commit succeeds only as a compare-and-swap:
the slot must still be free and its live version must still equal the version
the player read; it then stamps the player as owner and advances the version.
If the read version is stale, the player cannot commit and must retry, dropping
its request and counting the attempt. An owner may later release its slot,
advancing the version back to an even value.

Actions: Prepare (a free-request player reads a slot's version into its
request), Commit (a player whose read version still matches the live version
of a free slot becomes its owner and advances the version), Retry (a player
whose read version is now stale drops its request and records a retry), and
Release (an owner frees its slot and advances the version).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a slot has an owner if and only if its version is odd, so the
compare-and-swap can never let a stale request slip a second owner onto a slot
that is already allocated.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p1t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, MaxV, MaxVer, LoCap, HiCap

VARIABLES total, version, snapVal, snapVer, phase, cap

vars == <<total, version, snapVal, snapVer, phase, cap>>

Idle == "idle"
Armed == "armed"

TypeOK ==
    /\ total \in 0..MaxV
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snapVal \in [Banks -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ snapVer \in [Banks -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ phase \in [Banks -> {Idle, Armed}]
    /\ cap \in {LoCap, HiCap}

Init ==
    /\ total = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snapVal = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ snapVer = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [b \in Banks |-> Idle]
    /\ cap = HiCap

Snapshot(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = Idle
    /\ snapVal' = [snapVal EXCEPT ![b] = total]
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![b] = version]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = Armed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, version, cap>>

Committable(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = Armed
    /\ snapVer[b] = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ snapVal[b] + 1 <= cap
    /\ snapVal[b] + 1 <= MaxV

Commit(b) ==
    /\ Committable(b)
    /\ total' = snapVal[b] + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVal, snapVer, cap>>

Abort(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = Armed
    /\ ~Committable(b)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, version, snapVal, snapVer, cap>>

ChangeCap ==
    /\ cap' = IF cap = HiCap THEN LoCap ELSE HiCap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, version, snapVal, snapVer, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Snapshot(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Commit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Abort(b)
    \/ ChangeCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == total = version

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    MaxV = 3
    MaxVer = 3
    LoCap = 2
    HiCap = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
Scenario: a bank's interbank settlement batch

Two settlement banks post entries into one shared batch record that holds a
running total and a version counter. Coordination is optimistic locking with
retry, and crucially each post is a blind read-modify-write: a bank first
snapshots the record's total and version, and when it later posts it writes
back the snapshotted total plus one -- it does not re-read the live total.

That blind write is exactly where a lost update could occur. To prevent it,
a post commits only as a compare-and-swap: the version the bank snapshotted
must still equal the record's live version, proving no other post landed in
between. When it does, the total advances to the snapshot-plus-one and the
version advances by one. If another bank posted first, the snapshot is stale
and the compare-and-swap fails, so the bank aborts and must snapshot again.

Capacity changes at runtime: an operational cap on the batch total may be
raised or lowered between posts, and a post is refused when the new total
would exceed the current cap. A refused or stale-versioned attempt aborts.

Actions: Snapshot (an idle bank records the live total and version and arms a
post), Commit (an armed bank whose snapshot version is still live and whose
snapshot-plus-one is within the cap writes that value and advances the
version), Abort (an armed bank that cannot commit -- stale version or over
cap -- disarms), and ChangeCap (the runtime cap is set to a new value).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared total always equals the version counter, so no
blind post ever overwrote a concurrent post's contribution -- no update is
ever lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m9p0t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Procs, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, token, inCS, waiting, cap

vars == <<epoch, token, inCS, waiting, cap>>

NoTok == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ token \in Procs \cup {NoTok}
    /\ inCS \in [Procs -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ waiting \in [Procs -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ cap \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ token = NoTok
    /\ inCS = [p \in Procs |-> FALSE]
    /\ waiting = [p \in Procs |-> FALSE]
    /\ cap = 1

Request(p) ==
    /\ ~waiting[p]
    /\ token # p
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, token, inCS, cap>>

Acquire(p) ==
    /\ token = NoTok
    /\ waiting[p]
    /\ token' = p
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inCS, cap>>

Enter(p) ==
    /\ token = p
    /\ ~inCS[p]
    /\ cap >= 1
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, token, waiting, cap>>

Exit(p) ==
    /\ inCS[p]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ token' = NoTok
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, waiting, cap>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ token' = NoTok
    /\ inCS' = [p \in Procs |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, cap>>

ChangeCap ==
    /\ cap' = 1 - cap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, token, inCS, waiting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Request(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Acquire(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Enter(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Exit(p)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ ChangeCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion ==
    \A p \in Procs : inCS[p] => token = p

=============================================================================

    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
Scenario: a bank's interbank settlement batch

Three settlement processors contend for one critical resource: the exclusive
right to post to the live batch ledger. Access is governed by an
epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme. A single grant token names the process
currently entitled to the resource; only its holder may enter the critical
section.

A process first raises a request. When the token is free a requesting process
may acquire it. Holding the token is not the same as being inside: the holder
enters the critical section as a separate step, and only while capacity
permits. It leaves by exiting, which both clears its critical-section flag and
releases the token.

Reconfiguration is a hard barrier: bumping the configuration epoch revokes the
token and evicts every process from the critical section at once, so a
reconfiguration can never leave a stale holder inside. Capacity changes at
runtime: an admission capacity toggles between zero and one, and while it is
zero no process may enter, though held tokens and pending requests are
undisturbed.

Actions: Request (a process marks itself waiting), Acquire (a waiting process
takes the free token), Enter (the token holder enters the critical section
when capacity is at least one), Exit (the occupant leaves and releases the
token), Reconfigure (the epoch advances, revoking the token and evicting all
occupants), and ChangeCap (the admission capacity is set to zero or one).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a process is inside the critical section only if it currently
holds the single grant token, so at most one process ever occupies the
critical resource at a time.

nl:
Scenario: a hospital operating-room scheduler

Three scheduling processes contend for exclusive control of one operating
room, the critical resource. They coordinate with optimistic locking and
retry over a lock cell that carries an owner (a process, or "free") and a
version counter that advances on every acquire and every release.

To take the lock a process first reads the live version into a private
snapshot. It then attempts to acquire as a compare-and-swap: the lock must be
free and its live version must still equal the snapshot, proving nothing
changed since the read. A successful acquire names the process as owner and
advances the version; if the snapshot is stale the acquire simply is not
enabled and the process reads again to retry. Only the owner may enter the
room, and on exit it frees the lock and advances the version.

One participant can crash silently: a process may crash at any point, keeping
whatever it holds. Because a crashed owner can never exit on its own, the
scheduler may reclaim the room from a crashed owner -- and a correct reclaim
frees the lock and clears that owner's occupancy together, so the room is
never handed on while a crashed process is still recorded inside it.

Actions: Read (a process snapshots the live version), Acquire (a non-crashed
process whose snapshot still matches the free lock's version becomes owner and
advances the version), Enter (the owner enters the room), Exit (the owner
leaves, frees the lock, and advances the version), Crash (a process crashes
silently), and Reclaim (a crashed owner's lock is freed and its occupancy
cleared together).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a process occupies the operating room only if it is the
current owner of the lock, so at most one process is ever in the room at once.

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Three spooler workers compete for exclusive control of the single print head,
the critical resource. Ownership lives in one compare-and-swap register whose
value is the id of the current holder, or "free". A worker never writes the
register blindly: it first observes the register into a private expected
value, then attempts a compare-and-swap that succeeds only if the live
register still equals what it expected.

To take the head a worker observes "free" and swaps it to its own id; to
release it observes its own id and swaps it back to "free". Between observing
and swapping the register may have changed, in which case the expected value
no longer matches and the swap is not enabled, so the worker observes again.
Only a worker that has driven the register to its own id may run the head.

One participant can crash silently: a worker may crash while holding the head,
leaving the register pointing at it and its run flag set. Since a crashed
holder can neither swap nor stop, an operator reclaim resets the register to
"free" and clears that crashed worker's run flag in a single step, so the head
is never granted to another worker while a crashed one is still marked as
running it.

Actions: Observe (a worker copies the register into its expected value), Take
(a worker whose expected value is "free" swaps the free register to its id),

nl:
Scenario: a car-wash conveyor line

Two entry stations admit and release cars on a single conveyor line whose
occupancy is held in one compare-and-swap register: an integer count of cars
currently on the line. A station never adjusts the count blindly. It first
arms an intended operation -- an admit or a depart -- by snapshotting the live
count; it then performs the operation as a compare-and-swap that fires only if
the live count still equals the snapshot.

An admit fires only when the line is below the current capacity and bumps the
count up by one. A depart fires only when the line is non-empty, bumps the
count down by one, and records a completed wash. If the live count moved
between arming and firing, the snapshot is stale, the compare-and-swap is not
enabled, and the station retries by returning to idle.

Capacity changes at runtime: an operator may raise or lower the line capacity,
but capacity is never set below the cars already on the line -- you cannot
shrink the line under the cars occupying it.

ArmOut (an idle station snapshots the count to attempt a depart), Admit (an
in-armed station whose snapshot is still live and whose line is below capacity
increments the count), Depart (an out-armed station whose snapshot is still
live and whose line is non-empty decrements the count and records a wash),
Retry (an armed station whose snapshot went stale returns to idle), and
ChangeCap (the capacity is reset to a value no smaller than the current count).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cars on the conveyor line never exceeds the
current capacity.

nl:
Scenario: a wildfire drone surveillance swarm

Three drones maintain one shared map of confirmed fire sightings. Write access
is serialized by a token ring granting exclusive access: only the drone
currently holding the ring token may fold its sighting into the shared map.

Folding is a read-modify-write. When a drone captures the free token it
snapshots the current shared map into a private buffer. Later it merges by
writing back its snapshot together with its own sighting -- a blind write from
the snapshot, not a re-read of the live map. This is safe only because the
token grants exclusive access: while a drone holds the token no other drone
can have changed the map, so its snapshot is still current and nothing is
overwritten. After merging, the drone releases the token.

One participant can crash silently: a drone may crash while holding the token,
never merging and never releasing. To keep the ring alive an operator reclaim
regenerates the token from a crashed holder -- but a reclaim only frees the
token, it never performs a merge, so it can never blind-write a stale snapshot
over the map. At least one drone always stays alive.

Actions: Capture (a live drone takes the free token and snapshots the shared
map), Merge (the token holder writes its snapshot plus its own sighting into
the map, records the contribution, and releases the token), Crash (a drone
crashes silently while never leaving the last drone crashed), and Reclaim (a
crashed holder's token is regenerated without any merge).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every sighting that was ever contributed to the shared map is
still present in it, so no drone's update is ever silently lost by a blind
overwrite.

nl:
Scenario: a container-ship crane yard

Several yard cranes may move containers only when they hold a valid
authorization for the current control epoch. Authorization uses optimistic
locking with retry against a single authority epoch counter. To become
authorized a crane first reads the live authority epoch into a private
snapshot, then attempts a grant as a compare-and-swap: the grant records the
crane's authorized epoch only if the live authority epoch still equals the
snapshot. If the authority epoch advanced in between, the snapshot is stale,
the grant is refused, and the crane reads again to retry.

A crane may execute a move only while its recorded authorization epoch equals
the live authority epoch. The yard controller can revoke all authorizations by
advancing the authority epoch; a revoke also immediately halts every crane
currently moving, so no crane keeps acting on a superseded authorization.

One participant can crash silently: a crane may crash at any time; at least one
crane always remains live.

Actions: Read (a live crane snapshots the authority epoch), Grant (a live crane
whose snapshot still matches the live authority epoch records that epoch as its
authorization), Act (an authorized crane whose recorded epoch equals the live
authority epoch begins a move), Stop (a moving crane finishes its move), Revoke
(the authority epoch advances, halting all moving cranes), and Crash (a crane
crashes silently while never crashing the last live crane).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a crane is executing a move only if its recorded authorization
epoch equals the live authority epoch, so no stale or unauthorized crane ever
acts.

nl:
Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

Several grid controllers watch one feeder and may trip it to shed load. The
trip is irreversible: once the feeder breaker is open it stays open. Whether
the breaker is open lives in a single compare-and-swap register holding either
"closed" or "open".

A controller acts in stages so a slow controller cannot cause a double trip. It
first senses the register into a private read. If it read "closed" it may arm
an intent to shed. To actually shed it performs a compare-and-swap: the trip
fires only if the live register is still "closed", in which case it swaps the
register to "open" and records itself as the controller that opened the
breaker.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a controller may sense "closed", arm,
and then be delayed while a faster controller trips the feeder first. When the
slow controller finally looks, its compare-and-swap cannot fire because the
register is already "open", so it aborts its armed intent instead. No
controller is ever lost; each merely lags.

Actions: Sense (a controller reads the register into its private snapshot), Arm
(a controller that read "closed" arms an intent to shed), Shed (an armed
controller whose compare-and-swap finds the register still "closed" opens the
breaker and records itself as opener), and Abort (an armed controller that
finds the register already "open" drops its intent).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the feeder breaker is opened at most once across the entire
run, so the irreversible shed never happens twice.

nl:
Scenario: an elevator bank in a skyscraper

Two express elevators share one express shaft, the critical resource that only
one car may occupy at a time. A dispatcher, chosen by leader election with
failover, is the sole issuer of shaft grants. Each grant carries a sequence
number, and the dispatcher issues a new grant only when the shaft is empty,
naming the elevator entitled to enter and advancing the current grant sequence.

Grant messages can be reordered: the dispatcher's grants sit in a pending pool
and may be delivered to the cars in any order. A car acts on a grant only if
it is the current one -- the grant must name that car and its sequence number
must equal the live grant sequence. A grant whose sequence number is below the
live one is stale, a leftover from an earlier round, and is simply discarded
rather than acted upon. This is what makes reordering safe.

Leadership can fail over: any car may be elected dispatcher, superseding the
previous one.

the shaft is empty, advances the grant sequence, names an entitled car, and
emits a grant message), Enter (a car holding a current grant -- matching name
and live sequence -- enters the empty shaft and consumes the message),
StaleDrop (a grant message whose sequence is below the live sequence is
discarded), and Exit (the occupant leaves the shaft).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a car occupies the express shaft only if it is the car named
by the current grant, so at most one car is ever in the shaft at once.

nl:
Scenario: a wildfire drone surveillance swarm

Survey tasks are dispatched through a bounded work queue with backpressure.
Pending tasks sit in a queue that can hold at most a fixed number of entries;
when the queue is full, no new task may be enqueued -- that is the backpressure.
Two drones pull tasks. The dispatcher keeps an authoritative owner for every
task (a drone, or "free"), and each drone keeps a local claim naming the one
task it is currently working, if any.

A claim ties both sides together: pulling a queued task marks the task owned by
that drone and records the drone's claim, removing it from the queue.
Completing a task clears the drone's claim and frees the task's ownership,
marking it done. Done tasks may later be reopened for re-survey.

There is a privileged admin override. An administrator may forcibly reassign a
task from its current owner to another idle drone -- clearing the former
owner's claim and installing the new owner's claim in one atomic step -- or
force-clear a task back to free, again clearing its owner's stale claim at the
same time. The override budget is finite.

Actions: Enqueue (a free, not-done task joins the queue while it is below
capacity), Claim (an idle drone pulls a free queued task, taking ownership),
Complete (a drone finishes its claimed task, freeing it and marking it done),
Reopen (a done task is returned for re-survey), AdminReassign (the admin moves
an owned task to an idle drone, swapping claims atomically), and AdminClear
(the admin frees an owned task and clears its owner's claim atomically).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every drone that holds a claim is the authoritative owner of
the task it claims, so no task is ever double-allocated to two drones at once.

Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Two spooler workers append revisions to one shared spool record. Write access
uses lease-based ownership with expiry driven by a shared clock. A worker takes
a lease that names it the owner until an expiry time; only the current lease
holder, and only before its lease expires, may append a revision. The shared
record is the set of applied revision ids, which should always form a contiguous
run 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps.

Appending is a snapshot-then-write. When a worker acquires its lease it reads
the highest applied revision id into a private snapshot. To append it writes the
next id after its snapshot -- a blind increment from the snapshot -- but only if
its snapshot still equals the live highest id, so it never appends over a
revision another holder slipped in. The lease's exclusivity plus this check is
what keeps the run gap-free.

Time advances by ticks; when the clock passes a lease's expiry the lease is
gone and the record reverts to unowned, so a worker whose lease lapsed cannot
keep writing. Capacity changes at runtime: an append throughput cap toggles
between zero and one, and while it is zero no append may occur.

Actions: Acquire (an idle-lease worker takes a lease until now-plus-term and
snapshots the highest id), Tick (the clock advances), Write (the lease holder,
before expiry and with capacity, appends its snapshot-plus-one when the snapshot
is still the live highest id), Release (the holder gives up its lease), Expire
(a lease past its expiry is cleared), and ChangeCap (the append cap is set to
zero or one).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the set of applied revision ids is always downward closed --
every id above one has its predecessor present -- so no append ever skipped or
overwrote a revision, and no update was lost.

nl:
Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

Grid controllers may issue shed commands only under a current authorization
permit. The authority publishes one permit nonce; controllers obtain it with
optimistic locking and retry. A controller first reads the live permit nonce
into a private snapshot, then obtains authorization as a compare-and-swap: it
records the permit as its own only if the live permit still equals its snapshot;
otherwise it re-reads and retries.

An authorized controller submits shed commands into a shared pending set, each
command carrying the permit nonce it was issued under. A pending command is
executed only if its permit still equals the live permit. The authority may
reissue -- advancing the permit nonce -- when policy changes; a reissue clears
every outstanding pending command at once, so no command minted under an old
permit is left waiting to fire.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a controller may obtain a permit,
submit a command, and then lag while the authority reissues. Its submitted
command, now carrying a stale permit, is swept out by the reissue, and the slow
controller must read, obtain, and submit afresh. No controller is lost.

Actions: Read (a controller snapshots the live permit), Obtain (a controller
whose snapshot still matches the live permit records it as authorized), Submit
(an authorized controller emits a command tagged with the live permit), Apply (a
pending command whose permit still equals the live permit executes and is
removed), and Reissue (the permit advances and all pending commands are cleared).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every command still pending carries the current permit nonce,
so no stale or unauthorized command is ever left staged to act.

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Three spooler nodes edit one shared counter record -- the running total of
pages committed to the master spool. Write access is serialized by leader
election with failover: at most one node is leader, and each election takes a
strictly higher epoch so a superseded leader is replaced.

Only the current leader writes, and it writes blindly from a private snapshot
rather than re-reading the record. When a node is elected it snapshots the live
total into its own buffer. Each commit writes back its snapshot-plus-one and
advances its own snapshot in lockstep, so a healthy leader's snapshot stays
exactly equal to the live total. This is precisely what prevents a lost update:
a writer whose snapshot had drifted from the record would silently overwrite
another node's contribution, and leadership plus the snapshot discipline keep
that from happening.

One participant can crash silently: a node may crash while leader, after which
it can no longer commit. A new leader is elected at a higher epoch and takes a
fresh snapshot of the live total before it writes, so leadership always moves to
a node whose view of the record is current.

Actions: Elect (a node becomes leader at a higher epoch and snapshots the live
total), Write (a non-crashed leader commits its snapshot-plus-one, advancing the
total and its snapshot together), StepDown (the leader relinquishes leadership),
and Crash (a node crashes silently while the last live node is never crashed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever there is a leader, that leader's snapshot of the total
equals the live total, so no blind commit ever overwrites another node's update
-- no update is lost.

nl:
Scenario: an air-traffic runway allocator

One runway is the critical resource; at most one flight may be cleared onto it
at a time. Clearance is decided by two-phase commit across the tower's
controllers. A coordinator proposes a flight only while the runway is free,
opening a voting round in which every controller must vote. Because messages can
be reordered, controllers cast their votes in any order and at any time during
the round.

If all controllers vote yes, the round commits: the proposed flight takes the
runway and is marked cleared. If any controller votes no, the round aborts, the
proposal is dropped, and no flight is cleared. Once a cleared flight has landed,
the runway is freed and a new round may begin.

Actions: Propose (the coordinator, with a free runway, opens a voting round on a
flight and resets the ballots), Vote (a controller casts yes or no in the open
round -- votes may land in any order), Commit (a round with unanimous yes places
the proposed flight on the runway and marks it cleared), Abort (a round with any
no vote is dropped without clearing anyone), and Land (a cleared flight leaves,
freeing the runway).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a flight is marked cleared only if it is the flight currently
holding the runway, so at most one flight ever occupies the runway at a time.

Scenario: a hospital operating-room scheduler

Three scheduling nodes update one shared counter -- the running total of
confirmed room bookings. Write access rotates by a token ring granting exclusive
access: the token passes around a fixed ring, and only the node currently
holding the token may write.

Writing is a blind read-modify-write from a private snapshot. A node that has
just received the token must first snapshot the live total into its buffer; it
then commits by writing back its snapshot-plus-one, advancing a separate count
of committed writes in lockstep. Because the token grants exclusive access, no
other node changes the total while a node holds it, so the holder's snapshot
stays current and its blind write never clobbers another node's contribution.
A commit is refused unless the snapshot still equals the live total.

Capacity changes at runtime: a booking cap toggles between a low and a high
value, and no commit may push the total above the current cap.

Actions: Pass (the token holder hands the token to the next node in the ring),
Snapshot (the token holder reads the live total into its buffer), Write (the
holder, when its snapshot equals the live total and the total is below the cap,
commits its snapshot-plus-one and advances the committed-write count), and
ChangeCap (the booking cap is switched between low and high).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared total always equals the number of committed writes,
so no blind write ever overwrote another node's booking -- no update is lost.

nl:
Scenario: a smart-home door lock network

A fixed number of unlock credits circulate through the system; none are ever
created or destroyed, they only move between holding places. Two independent
lock-controller instances share one common credit pool. Each instance drives its
credits through a bounded work queue with backpressure and then into active
locks and back out.

A credit at any moment sits in exactly one place: the shared free pool, an
instance's bounded queue, an instance's active set, or an instance's releasing
set. An instance enqueues a credit by drawing one from the shared pool into its
queue, but only while its queue is below capacity -- that is the backpressure. A
queued credit is activated into a held lock; a held lock begins releasing; and a
releasing credit completes, returning to the shared pool for anyone to reuse.

Because both instances draw from and return to the same pool, the pool couples
them, yet every transition just relocates one credit and leaves the grand total
untouched.

Actions: Enqueue (an instance moves one credit from the shared pool into its
queue while below capacity), Activate (an instance moves one queued credit into
its active set), BeginRelease (an instance moves one active credit into its
releasing set), and Complete (an instance returns one releasing credit to the
shared pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared pool plus every credit queued, active, or releasing
across both instances always sums to the fixed total, so no credit is ever
created or destroyed.

Scenario: a blood-bank inventory tracker

Three technicians contend for exclusive use of the single cross-match bench,
the critical resource. Access is governed by lease-based ownership with expiry
against a shared clock. A technician acquires a lease that names it holder until
an expiry time; only the current holder, and only before its lease expires, may
occupy the bench.

Acquiring the lease is separate from entering: a holder enters the bench as its
own step while its lease is still in force, and on exit it both leaves the bench
and drops the lease. Time advances by ticks. When the clock reaches a lease's
expiry the lease lapses: the holder is cleared and, as a hard barrier, anyone at
the bench is evicted, so an expired lease never leaves a stale occupant behind.

One participant can crash silently: a technician may crash while holding the
lease -- even while at the bench -- and can then neither exit nor renew. The
clock still advances, the lease still expires on schedule, and expiry both
clears the crashed holder and evicts it from the bench. At least one technician
always stays live.

(the holder occupies the bench while the lease is still in force), Exit (the
occupant leaves and drops the lease), Tick (the clock advances), Expire (a lease
at or past its expiry is cleared and its occupant evicted), and Crash (a
technician crashes silently while the last live technician is never crashed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a technician occupies the bench only if it is the current lease
holder, so at most one technician is ever at the bench at a time.

Scenario: a pharmacy prescription dispenser

A fixed number of controlled-drug units circulate through the pharmacy; none are
ever created or destroyed, they only move between the shared stock, a
pharmacist's hand, and the dispensed tally. Two pharmacists move units and
coordinate on the shared stock count with optimistic locking and retry.

Moving a unit out of stock is a blind read-modify-write. A pharmacist first
reads the stock count into a private snapshot, then takes a unit by writing back
its snapshot-minus-one -- it does not re-read the live count. The take commits
only as a compare-and-swap: the live stock must still equal the snapshot, so two
pharmacists can never both decrement from the same reading and conjure or lose a
unit. A taken unit is held, then dispensed. A dispensed unit can be returned to
stock, again as a snapshot-plus-one compare-and-swap.

One participant can crash silently: a pharmacist may crash while holding a unit;
the unit stays counted in its hand and is never lost. At least one pharmacist
always stays live.

Actions: Read (a pharmacist snapshots the live stock count), Take (a pharmacist
whose snapshot still matches the live stock moves one unit from stock into its
hand), Dispense (a pharmacist moves one held unit into the dispensed tally),
Return (a pharmacist whose snapshot still matches the live stock moves one unit
from the dispensed tally back into stock), and Crash (a pharmacist crashes
silently while the last live pharmacist is never crashed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the stock plus every unit held by a pharmacist plus the
dispensed tally always sums to the fixed total, so no unit is ever created or
destroyed by a stale update.

    /\ acting = [c \in Ctrls |-> NoAct]
    /\ requested = [c \in Ctrls |-> FALSE]

Request(c) ==
    /\ ~requested[c]
    /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, acting>>

AcquireCoarse(c) ==
    /\ requested[c]
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ coarse' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, acting, requested>>

AcquireFine(c, f) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ fine[f] = Free
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![f] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, acting, requested>>

Act(c, f) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ fine[f] = c
    /\ acting[c] = NoAct
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![c] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, requested>>

Stop(c) ==
    /\ acting[c] # NoAct
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![c] = NoAct]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, requested>>

ReleaseFine(c, f) ==
    /\ fine[f] = c
    /\ acting[c] # f
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![f] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, acting, requested>>

ReleaseCoarse(c) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ acting[c] = NoAct
    /\ \A f \in Feeders : fine[f] # c
    /\ coarse' = Free
    /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, acting>>

Revoke ==
    /\ coarse' = Free
    /\ fine' = [f \in Feeders |-> Free]
    /\ acting' = [c \in Ctrls |-> NoAct]
    /\ UNCHANGED requested

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Request(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : AcquireCoarse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, f \in Feeders : AcquireFine(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, f \in Feeders : Act(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Stop(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, f \in Feeders : ReleaseFine(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : ReleaseCoarse(c)
    \/ Revoke

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Authorized ==
    \A c \in Ctrls : acting[c] # NoAct =>
        (coarse = c /\ fine[acting[c]] = c)

=============================================================================
nl:
Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

Two controllers may shed load on two feeders, but only under a strict
hierarchical locking discipline: coarse then fine. There is one shared coarse
lock -- the single region pool that both feeder instances draw from -- and a
separate fine lock for each feeder. A controller must first hold the coarse
region lock, and only then may it take a feeder's fine lock. It may act on a
feeder only while it holds both the coarse lock and that feeder's fine lock.

Because the two feeder instances share the one coarse pool, the controllers
contend for it, and the ordering (coarse before fine) prevents a controller from
touching a feeder it is not fully entitled to. A region-wide revoke can clear
every lock and halt all shedding at once, so no controller keeps acting on
authority that has been pulled out from under it.

Actions: Request (a controller marks that it wants access), AcquireCoarse (a
requesting controller takes the free coarse pool lock), AcquireFine (a coarse
holder takes a free feeder's fine lock), Act (a controller holding both the
coarse lock and a feeder's fine lock begins shedding that feeder), Stop (a
controller stops shedding), ReleaseFine (a controller not acting on a feeder
releases its fine lock), ReleaseCoarse (a controller holding no fine locks and
not acting releases the coarse pool), and Revoke (all locks are cleared and all
shedding halted at once).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a controller sheds a feeder only if it currently holds both the
shared coarse pool lock and that feeder's fine lock, so no unauthorized or stale
controller ever acts.

    /\ budget = MaxOverride

    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[clerk |-> w, rv |-> version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, base, budget>>

    /\ r.rv = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ base' = r.rv
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED budget

Discard(r) ==

    /\ (r.rv # version \/ version = MaxVer)
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, base, budget>>

AdminApply(r) ==
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ base' = version
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ budget' = budget - 1

    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Discard(r)

nl:
Scenario: a blood-bank inventory tracker

Two clerks revise one shared inventory record that carries a version counter and
the base version its most recent revision was built upon. Revisions flow through
a bounded work queue with backpressure: prepared revision requests wait in a
queue that holds at most a fixed number of entries, and no new request may be
prepared once the queue is full.

A prepared request records the version it was read against. Applying it is a
compare-and-swap: the revision commits only if the version it read still equals
the live version, in which case the live version advances by one and the record
stamps the read version as the new base. A request whose read version is stale
-- or that cannot commit because the record is already at its maximum -- is
discarded and must be prepared again. This read-check is exactly what stops one
clerk's revision from silently overwriting another's.

There is a privileged admin override: an administrator may force a queued
request to commit even without a matching read version, but the override still
stamps the base correctly as the version just superseded, so a forced revision
never corrupts the record's lineage. The override budget is finite.

Actions: Prepare (a clerk queues a request tagged with the live version while the
queue is below capacity), Apply (a queued request whose read version still
matches the live version commits, advancing the version and stamping its read as
base), Discard (a queued request that cannot commit is dropped), and AdminApply
(the admin forces a queued request to commit, advancing the version and stamping
the superseded version as base).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the record has been revised at least once, its base
equals exactly one less than its live version, so every revision built on the
immediately preceding one and no update was lost.

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Two independent print instances -- queue A with two workers and queue B with two
workers -- share one token ring granting exclusive access to the single print
head. Exactly one token circulates the shared ring across all four workers, so
the two instances draw from one common pool. A worker may print only while it
holds the token.

A worker that wants to print first raises a request. Only the current token
holder may begin printing. The token passes around the ring to the next worker,
but a holder may pass only when it is not currently printing, so the token never
slips away from a worker mid-job. When a worker finishes, it stops printing and
records the completed job.

Because the token moves only from an idle holder and printing requires holding
the token, a worker whose token has moved on cannot keep printing, and a worker
that never held the token cannot print at all.

Actions: Request (a worker marks that it wants to print), Pass (an idle token
holder hands the token to the next worker in the shared ring), Act (a requesting
token holder begins printing), and Finish (a printing worker stops and records a
completed job).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a worker is printing only if it currently holds the single ring
token, so no unauthorized or stale worker ever drives the print head.

    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ holder' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, inVault, budget>>

    /\ ~inVault[m]
    /\ inVault' = [inVault EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, holder, budget>>

Exit(m) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch>>

    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ holder' = m
    /\ budget' = budget - 1

    \/ \E m \in Machines : Enter(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Exit(m)

nl:
Scenario: a vending machine network

Three machines in a network share one refill vault, the critical resource that
only one machine may open at a time. A dispatcher, chosen by leader election
with failover, grants the vault lock. Each election takes a strictly higher
epoch, so a superseded dispatcher is replaced.

The dispatcher grants the vault lock to a machine only when the lock is free.
Holding the lock is not the same as being inside: the holder opens the vault as
a separate step, and on close it both leaves the vault and releases the lock.

There is a privileged admin override. An administrator may force-evict a
machine, clearing the vault lock and that machine's open state together in one
step, or force-grant the free vault lock to a machine directly, bypassing the
dispatcher. The override budget is finite, and every override preserves the
lock-and-occupant coupling so it can never strand two machines in the vault.

Actions: Elect (a machine becomes dispatcher at a higher epoch), Grant (the
dispatcher grants the free vault lock to a machine), Enter (the lock holder
opens the vault), Exit (the occupant closes the vault and releases the lock),
AdminEvict (the admin clears the lock and its occupant together), and AdminGrant
(the admin grants the free lock to a machine directly).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a machine has the vault open only if it currently holds the
vault lock, so at most one machine is ever in the vault at a time.
